title: Stratified finite-free calculation for completed rational pullback
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $\ell$ a prime invertible in $k$, and $X$ a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Fix an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and finite intermediate fields $E\subset L$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Write $A_E=\mathcal O_E$, choose a uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and put $B_{E,X}=\varprojlim_{n\ge1}(A_E/\varpi_E^n)_X$ and $E_X=B_{E,X}[1/\varpi_E]$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. These are the continuous completed coefficient sheaves on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use the derived-complete constructible integral categories with compatible etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], their raw rationalizations $D^b_c(X,E)$ [def-weil-pbc-rational-category], their bounded localized standard t-structures [prop-weil-localized-tstructure], and the pair category $D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], with the finite scalar functors $T_{L/E}$ and associators of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension].

Let $Y$ also be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme and let $g:Y\to X$ be any scheme morphism. For $\Lambda=E$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, use the finite-stage or common-stage standard structure, respectively [lem-per-adic-common-stage-truncations]. The completed integral pullback [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] preserves the constructible complete categories, including their finite reduction witnesses; it rationalizes to an exact triangulated functor and has coherent comparisons with finite scalar extension, including the unit, composition and shift equations. Its common-stage descent is likewise an exact triangulated functor $Lg^*:D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)\to D^b_c(Y,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$.

At a finite stage, let $J_X$ be the continuous rational realization [lem-per-continuous-rational-derived-realization]. If $F$ is a constructible $E_X$-module sheaf, and $S\hookrightarrow X$ is any stratum on which it is locally finite free, the restriction of $J_Y(Lg^*J_X^{-1}F)$ to $Y\times_X S$ is concentrated in degree zero. On the pullback of any pro-etale chart trivializing $F|_S$ as $E_S^r$, it is the finite free continuous target module of rank $r$ in degree zero, with its balanced-tensor identification. These assertions include empty strata and rank zero and impose no flatness hypothesis on $g^{-1}E_X\to E_Y$.

Consequently $Lg^*$ preserves the standard heart and both standard halves for both $\Lambda$. More generally it preserves every cohomological interval. Its restriction to the heart is exact, and the canonical truncation comparisons identify $\mathcal H^j(Lg^*K)$ with $g^*\mathcal H^j(K)$ for every integer $j$, compatibly with the finite scalar comparisons.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2, Definitions 6.8.6 and 6.8.8, Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15; completed pullback, local finite-free calculation and bounded truncation devissage

proof.text: Both $X$ and $Y$ satisfy the noetherian and finite-dimensional hypotheses of the cited adic results. Apply the finite-type noetherian theorem to their structure maps to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ (a field is noetherian). Apply the finite-type fibre dimension bound to the same maps: their unique fibres are $X$ and $Y$. The base is quasi-compact. Invertibility of $\ell$ is inherited from $k$. No smoothness, flatness or assumption that $k$ is algebraically closed is used.

source.place: Hypotheses of Proposition 6.6.11 and Remark 6.8.15; scheme-hypothesis verification

proof.text: Write $\mathcal C_W=D^b_c(W,A_E)$ with exactly the compatible etale-origin witnesses in the statement. The integral stratified-perfect characterization identifies this category with the detailed integral category used by the chart lemmas, with the same completed ring and reduction functors. The rational-realization pullback comparison states that ordinary ringed pullback $P_g$ preserves $\mathcal C$ and that the specified quotient-tower unit $\gamma_g:P_gK\to\widehat P_gK$ is invertible; it also retains the compatible etale witnesses. Thus the actual completed pullback restricts to $\mathcal C_X\to\mathcal C_Y$. The completed-pullback triangle theorem supplies its shift comparison and preservation of distinguished triangles. These are inherited ambient triangles, not newly chosen triangles. The functor is $A_E$-linear by the chart-restriction lemma (equivalently its scalar action on all quotient-tower maps).

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9(4)-(5), Proposition 6.6.11; specified-unit comparison supplied by the cited DAG lemma

proof.text: Fix integral $K$ with ambient cohomology supported in a finite interval $[a,b]$. The chart-restriction lemma supplies a finite locally closed stratification $S_\alpha$ and pro-etale covers $V_{\alpha t}\to S_\alpha$ on which $K$ is $C_V(P)=B_{E,V}\otimes_{\underline{A_E}}\underline{P^\bullet}$ for bounded finite-projective $A_E$-complexes $P^\bullet$. Its exact restriction assertion puts each such model in $[a,b]$. Set $S'_\alpha=Y\times_XS_\alpha$, $V'_{\alpha t}=Y\times_XV_{\alpha t}$ and $g_{\alpha t}:V'_{\alpha t}\to V_{\alpha t}$. The same lemma states that the nonempty $S'_\alpha$ stratify $Y$, the $V'_{\alpha t}$ cover them pro-etale, and the restriction of $\widehat P_gK$ is the specified completed pullback of this model along $g_{\alpha t}$. In particular we take fibre-product strata, not a factorization deduced merely from inclusion of images.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11, Lemma 6.5.8 and Remark 6.5.10; chart and restriction part

proof.text: Apply the completed perfect scalar-pullback calculation on every $g_{\alpha t}$. It gives $Lg_{\alpha t}^*C_V(P)\cong C_{V'}(P)$, with the actual finite quotient projections and transitions. Its cohomology and balanced-tensor assertions give $\mathcal H^jC_{V'}(P)\cong g_{\alpha t}^*\mathcal H^jC_V(P)$ and therefore zero for $j\notin[a,b]$. The exact restrictions in the previous step identify these sheaves with the restrictions of $\mathcal H^j(\widehat P_gK)$. Apply noetherian stratum detection on $Y$ to each such abelian sheaf to obtain global vanishing. Empty strata contribute nothing; if $K=0$ the additive functor sends it to zero, covering an empty interval. Finally the integral standard t-structure is bounded and its halves are defined by ambient vanishing: for an integral nonpositive object choose a bound $[a,0]$, and for a nonnegative one choose $[0,b]$. The same argument proves preservation of both integral halves. This checks the crucial hypothesis of coefficient-stage descent, without assuming flatness of $g^{-1}B_{E,X}\to B_{E,Y}$.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.9(4)-(5) and Proposition 6.6.11, local perfect-model calculation followed by vanishing detection; Stacks Tags 093M, 09AH and 09AB through the cited lemmas

proof.text: Rationalize the $A_E$-linear exact functor using semilinear scalar localization with $R=S=A_E$ and $t=u=\varpi_E$: on a fraction it is $f/\varpi_E^n\mapsto\widehat P_g(f)/\varpi_E^n$. The localized t-structure has exactly the image halves required by descent. The scalar-extension package gives the completed integral comparison $C_{L/E,Y}\widehat P_{g,E}\cong\widehat P_{g,L}C_{L/E,X}$ and its identity, composition, coefficient-tower and shift equations. Since Step 2 proved constructible preservation, these comparisons restrict here, and semilinear localization preserves their equations. Thus they are the exact rational-stage comparisons $\beta_{L/E}:T_{L/E,Y}F_E\cong F_LT_{L/E,X}$, with their stated unit and associator normalizations.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2) and Remark 6.8.15; raw scalar localization and the specified coherent scalar package

proof.text: Apply coefficient-stage descent with integral categories $\mathcal C_X,\mathcal C_Y$ and integral functors $\widehat P_{g,E}$ for every finite field $E$. Step 2 gives linear exactness, Step 4 gives preservation of integral halves, and Step 5 gives the exact scalar comparisons. The common-stage truncation theorem supplies t-exact transitions and the bounded common-stage t-structures with finite-stage truncations; the scalar-extension package supplies exact transition functors with literal identities and associators; the pair-category definition supplies the same common-stage morphisms and cone triangles (a triangle is distinguished iff isomorphic to the image of one finite-stage triangle), and the Verdier-axioms theorem proves that these data form a triangulated category. These are precisely the remaining hypotheses of descent. Consequently each rational $F_E$ and the functor $F_{\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell}$ are exact and t-exact. Explicitly the latter sends $(E,K)$ to $(E,F_EK)$ and sends a common-stage arrow $u$ over $L$ to $\beta_{\mathrm{target}}^{-1}F_L(u)\beta_{\mathrm{source}}$. The unit and tower equations proved in Step 5 make this independent of further enlargement, as asserted by descent. This constructs the requested common-stage pullback, with its actual arrow action.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(1)-(2); abstract coefficient-stage descent applied to the actual pair categories

proof.text: For the additional finite-stage local formula, use $J$ to write the realized pullback of a constructible module sheaf $F$ as $G_gF=E_Y\otimes^L_{g^{-1}E_X}g^{-1}F$. Let $i:S\hookrightarrow X$ be the chosen stratum and $i':S'=Y\times_XS\hookrightarrow Y$. Their coefficient maps are isomorphisms and their pullbacks are exact restrictions, by continuous rational realization. Composition for ambient ringed derived pullbacks identifies $i'^*G_gF$ with $G_{g_S}i^*F$, since $g i'=i g_S$; the structural coefficient maps agree by the finite quotient normalization. On a pro-etale chart $v:U\to S$, put $U'=S'\times_SU$. Slice normalization identifies its restriction with $G_{g_U}(F|_U)$, where $g_U:U'\to U$. This uses restriction for a site object, so imposes no noetherian hypothesis on $U$ or $U'$.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2, Definitions 6.8.6 and 6.8.8, Remark 6.8.15; restriction and balanced composition

proof.text: On a chart trivializing $F|_S$ as $E_U^r$, the derived pullback unit $G_{g_U}(E_U)\cong E_{U'}$ and additivity give $G_{g_U}(E_U^r)\cong E_{U'}^r[0]$. The balanced-tensor map is $e'\otimes(e_1,\ldots,e_r)\mapsto(e'g_U^\sharp(e_1),\ldots,e'g_U^\sharp(e_r))$; its inverse sends the $j$-th basis vector with coefficient $a$ to $a\otimes e_j$. These are inverse by the balancing relation. For $r=0$ both sides are zero. Since pro-etale restriction is exact, all nonzero-degree cohomology sheaves restrict to zero on this cover and hence are zero; alternatively apply stratum detection to the one-stratum scheme $S'$ with these charts. Thus the restriction to $S'$ is concentrated in degree zero, with exactly the asserted continuous finite free chart model. For empty $S'$ this assertion is vacuous. The calculation uses only the derived pullback unit, not flatness of its coefficient map.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; finite direct sum of the derived tensor unit and its explicit balanced-tensor formula

proof.text: The descent theorem gives exactness on both hearts and the canonical truncation comparisons $\alpha^-:F\tau^{\le m}\cong\tau^{\le m}F$ and $\alpha^+:F\tau^{\ge m}\cong\tau^{\ge m}F$, characterized by their counit and unit equations. It also gives $F\mathcal H^j\cong\mathcal H^jF$ and compatibility with every $\beta_{L/E}$. On a heart object define $g^*=F|_{\mathrm{heart}}$; invert this cohomology comparison to get $\mathcal H^j(Lg^*K)\cong g^*\mathcal H^j(K)$ in the direction in the statement. Preservation of every interval is just preservation of the intersection $D^{\ge a}\cap D^{\le b}$, using t-exactness and the shift comparisons; an empty interval contains only zero. These conclusions hold at each finite stage and on the common-stage category by the same theorem.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14 and Remark 6.8.15; uniqueness-normalized truncation and cohomology consequences of the cited descent theorem
